title: The Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1968-08-22
lineage: Master Reel > ? > DAT > Panasonic SV-3700 > Korg MR-1 DSD [1 Bit/2.8 Mhz] Mastering: AudioGate to [24/96] > WaveLab > Nomad Blue Tube Limiter LM2S-3 >  AudioGate to [16/44.1] > CD Wave > TLH > Flac

ai_review.summary: High‑energy late‑summer ’68 set with a smoking Dark Star and Other One captured on a solid soundboard source.
ai_review.review: The Koucky tape delivers a strong second‑half performance from the August 1968 run, highlighted by a tight St. Stephen, a duel‑style Eleven, a superb Dark Star, and a fire‑blazing Other One that rolls into New Potato. The soundboard recording is generally clear with only minor vocal level quirks, making it an enjoyable listen despite being less complete than the Cotsman version.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers praise the musical performance (high energy, many standout jams) and note a decent soundboard capture; only one brief negative/irrelevant review limits confidence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear overall soundboard mix; occasional low vocal volume in St. Stephen but no major drop‑outs or distortion reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth transitions from St. Stephen into The Eleven, then a seamless move to Death Don't Have No Mercy; the second half builds momentum through Dark Star and culminates with an energetic Other One > New Potato sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocal volume low at start but powerful later; guitar duels with Phil in The Eleven and leads a masterful Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Phil: Engaged, "zooming" bass lines; extended solo on New Potato, strong interplay with Jerry throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ embellishments praised as perfect during Death Don't Have No Mercy.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann described as "going nuts" on drums, driving the high‑energy jams.
